children: Super Micro Computer reported a near-fourfold increase in revenue for the most recent quarter as customers continued spending heavily on artificial-intelligence infrastructure.
The server company on Tuesday reported a fiscal first-quarter profit of $1.59 billion, or $1.75 a share. That compares with a profit of $168.3 million, or 26 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were $1.81 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting $1.23 a share.

Revenue rose to $19.95 billion, up from $5.02 billion a year prior, and beating analysts' expectations for $17.53 billion. Last month, Super Micro lifted its revenue guidance for the quarter to a range of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, up $4 billion from its previous view.

"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate," Chief Executive Officer Charles Liang said. "Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, superior up-time and more cost-effective for our customer base."
For the current fiscal year, the company guided for revenue between $72 billion and $82 billion. Analysts currently expect $73.03 billion for the year.
The company's projection includes between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion of revenue during the fiscal second quarter, above analyst expectations for $18.11 billion.
Second-quarter earnings per share for the quarter are expected to be $1.59 to $1.83 per share. Adjusted earnings are expected between $1.66 and $1.90 a share. Analysts currently expect $1.14 a share.
Shares gained 5.7% to $33.19 in after-hours trading on Tuesday. The stock closed up 3.1% at $31.39, and was up 7.2% year-to-date through the close.
Earlier this month, the company named Mark Long as its next chief financial officer, ending a nearly two-year search to fill the role.

Super Micro also recently completed an investigation into an alleged scheme to smuggle Nvidia chips into China. The company said in August that the independent board investigation cleared its current senior management team. Earlier in the year, co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw resigned from the company after being indicted for his alleged role in the scheme.
